agent.final_message:
I did not prove P1.Insertion (L2). The proof file deliberately has no `Candidate.main`, so `viridis-lean-check` stops with "missing `theorem main`" and the claim will not be PROVEN. What I did do is reduce L2 to one stated gap, with everything else proved in Lean. The file is about 1,600 lines, compiles in about 20 seconds, and the main theorems use only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.

**Proved in Lean, no gaps (`out/proofs/P1.Insertion.lean`)**
- **The three ingredients of the insertion step:**
  - the change in χ depends only on the 3×3 window around p (`euler_insert_local`);
  - C8 changes by 1 − k, where k is the number of barrier components touching p (`C8_insert`);
  - the enclosed count changes only through p's old region and the new pieces next to p (`enclosed_insert`).
- **Finiteness:** every finite raster has finitely many enclosed regions (`finite_enclosed`).
- **Scan-order reduction:** it is enough to handle pixels added in raster-scan order (`statement_of_scan`). There, four of the five neighbourhood cases close by local arguments.
- **The fifth case is a digital Jordan lemma:** S's region is enclosed exactly when the left neighbour and SE are connected in B. I proved one direction (connected ⇒ enclosed) by a crossing-parity argument (`senc_of_join`).
- **Half of the bridge identity:** enc(B) ≥ C8(B) − χ(B) for every finite raster (`invariant_nonneg`). This follows because each scan-order insertion changes the invariant by 0 or +1.
- **Special case:** L2 holds when all four 4-neighbours of p are barrier (`insertion_hole`).

**The one remaining gap:** the other direction of the Jordan lemma (S's region enclosed ⇒ left neighbour and SE connected). Equivalently, enc ≤ C8 − χ. `statement_of_enc_join` and `statement_of_le` derive L2 from it. It needs a boundary-following argument or the "border of a finite region is 8-connected" lemma, which I didn't attempt. Changing the insertion order can't avoid it: the four-pixel diamond lands in this case under every scan order.

**Evidence, not proof:** `code/core_check.py` checks the full Jordan lemma (both directions) on 17,344 configurations with no failures. It also checks 15,281 scan-order insertions with no failures. A deliberately broken version of the check reports 3,662 failures, so the test can tell the cases apart.
